bugs.error_message: Datadog showed 'set Datadog keys in Settings' but the key inputs were hidden until the source toggle was on
bugs.root_cause: Secret rows were gated on src.enabled, so unavailable sources had no way to set keys before enabling
bugs.fix: Always render secret fields for sources that declare them, independent of the enabled toggle

bugs.error_message: Release workflow run succeeded and packaged archives/SBOMs but created no GitHub Release
bugs.root_cause: The only Release run was a workflow_dispatch on main, so github.ref_type was 'branch'. The args expression selected 'release --snapshot --clean', which builds and packages into dist/ but never publishes; the attestation step was skipped by the same condition. There was no way for a manual run to publish.
bugs.fix: Added an optional workflow_dispatch 'tag' input. A job-level RELEASE_TAG env resolves to github.ref_name on a v* tag push or the dispatch input otherwise; when non-empty the job checks out that tag, runs 'release --clean' with GORELEASER_CURRENT_TAG, and attests provenance. Empty still means a snapshot dry run, now uploading dist as a 'snapshot-dist' artifact.

bugs.error_message: Could not push tag v0.1.0: 'error: RPC failed; HTTP 403' on git-receive-pack for refs/tags/*
bugs.root_cause: A Claude Code remote session's git credentials permit branch pushes (claude/*) but refuse refs/tags/*. Separately, the obvious workaround — creating the release in the GitHub Releases UI — is unsafe with immutable releases enabled: it publishes instantly, so GoReleaser cannot attach assets and the tag name is permanently burnt.
bugs.fix: Added a create_tag checkbox to the Release workflow's workflow_dispatch so the job mints the tag and releases it in one run. Added replace_existing_draft so a mid-upload failure can be retried, and tightened tag validation to a real semver regex since a bad tag would otherwise be pushed before GoReleaser rejects it.

bugs.error_message: release failed after 6m2s - failed to upload triage_0.1.0_linux_i386.rpm.spdx.json: 422 Validation Failed [{Resource:ReleaseAsset Field:name Code:already_exists}]
bugs.root_cause: release.extra_files globbed dist/*.spdx.json, but GoReleaser already uploads every SBOM-typed artifact to the release. All 42 SBOMs were therefore queued twice and the duplicate POST returned 422 already_exists. Snapshot runs never upload, so 4 green snapshot runs could not catch it - it only surfaced on the first real tagged release.
bugs.fix: Removed release.extra_files. checksum.extra_files stays: it only adds the SBOMs as checksums.txt subjects (so provenance covers them) and uploads nothing.

bugs.error_message: Re-running the Release workflow for existing tag v0.1.0 would have reproduced the identical '422 already_exists' SBOM failure even though the fix was already merged to main (caught from the run's head_sha and cancelled before it built)
bugs.root_cause: Publishing an already-existing tag checks out THAT TAG (ref: env.RELEASE_TAG), and GoReleaser reads .goreleaser.yaml from the checked-out tree. Tag v0.1.0 pointed at ff9f062, which predates the PR #13 fix, so the tag's tree still carried the broken release.extra_files glob. A fix merged to main is invisible to a release cut from an older tag. Only the workflow YAML itself comes from the dispatched ref; all repository content comes from the checkout.
bugs.fix: Cut v0.1.1 from main with create_tag=true instead. That path checks out main (which has the fix) and creates the tag there, so GoReleaser reads the corrected config. A tag whose tree contains a broken release config cannot be repaired by fixing main - only by deleting and re-creating the tag, or by moving to a new version number.
